chunks: I had intended to appoint Hāshim ibn ‘Utbah as governor of Egypt, and had I done so, he would not have left the field open for them, nor allowed them the opportunity (to capture him). This is without reproach to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, for he was dear to me and I had brought him up.

key_terms.أَنْهَزَهُمُ الْفُرْصَة: to let them seize the opportunity
key_terms.الْعَرْصَة: the field/open ground (metaphor for opportunity or space to act)
key_terms.تَوْلِيَة: appointment to a position of authority

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali choose Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr over Hashim ibn Utbah for the governorship of Egypt?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) explains that he chose Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr for his political acumen and ability to secure Egypt against rivals, rather than for lack of merit in Hāshim ibn ‘Utbah. This decision highlights the Shia principle of *siyāsah* (pragmatic governance) where administrative competence is prioritized, while affirming the deep personal bond and familial closeness (*ribābah*) Ali maintained with Muḥammad.
